classification.difficultyReason: Convert successive true bearings into the included triangle angle, then apply the cosine rule.

content.prompt: A hiker walks 5 km on a bearing of $143^{\circ}\mathrm{T}$ and then turns on a bearing of $121^{\circ}\mathrm{T}$ and walks a further 10 km. How far is the hiker from his starting position? Give your answer correct to one decimal place.

answer.worked:
Let $A$ be the starting position, $B$ the turning point and $C$ the final position. The reverse bearing of $A$ from $B$ is $323^{\circ}\mathrm{T}$, so the interior angle at $B$ is

$$\angle ABC=360^{\circ}-(323^{\circ}-121^{\circ})=158^{\circ}.$$

Using the cosine rule:

$$\begin{align*}AC^2&=5^2+10^2-2(5)(10)\cos158^{\circ}\\AC&=\sqrt{125-100\cos158^{\circ}}\\AC&\approx14.8\text{ km}\end{align*}$$
